$comment: Licence policy of the FOSS compliance line (scripts/foss/foss.mjs, REQ-LTTCE-FOS-00004). Lattice is offered under AGPL-3.0-or-later and, alternatively, under a commercial licence, so every shipped third-party component must fit BOTH. A licence not listed in any category is 'review' and fails the gate until it is classified here or excepted below.

obligation.MPL-2.0: File-level copyleft (MPL-2.0 section 3): these files stay under MPL-2.0, and their source form must remain available to recipients. Lattice does not modify them; the source is at the location given.

obligation.LGPL-2.0-or-later: Library loaded at run time as a separate, replaceable file: recipients may replace it with a modified version; its source is offered (see the written offer); Lattice's terms do not forbid reverse engineering for debugging such modifications.
obligation.LGPL-2.1-only: Library loaded at run time as a separate, replaceable file: recipients may replace it with a modified version; its source is offered (see the written offer); Lattice's terms do not forbid reverse engineering for debugging such modifications.
obligation.LGPL-2.1-or-later: Library loaded at run time as a separate, replaceable file: recipients may replace it with a modified version; its source is offered (see the written offer); Lattice's terms do not forbid reverse engineering for debugging such modifications.
obligation.LGPL-3.0-or-later: Library loaded at run time as a separate, replaceable file: recipients may replace it with a modified version; its source is offered (see the written offer); Lattice's terms do not forbid reverse engineering for debugging such modifications.
obligation.MPL-1.1: File-level copyleft: these files stay under MPL-1.1 and their source is offered (see the written offer).

obligation.LGPL-2.1-only: Statically linked into a separate program (the AppImage runtime) that Lattice's code does not link with: that program's complete source and build scripts are public, so it can be rebuilt with a modified library; its source is offered (see the written offer).

$comment_separateProgram: Applies ONLY to components with linkage 'separate-program': programs of their own inside the Linux AppImage that Lattice's executable does not link with — the AppImage runtime and the libraries statically linked into it, AppRun (foss/extra-components.json, REQ-LTTCE-FOS-00006). Lattice is merely aggregated with them, so their licence does not reach Lattice's code; the LGPL's relinking duty concerns the runtime, whose source (MIT) is public.
$comment_sharedLibrary: Applies ONLY to components with linkage 'shared-library': system libraries the Linux AppImage carries as separate files the dynamic linker loads at run time (foss/appimage-packages.json, REQ-LTTCE-FOS-00006). There the LGPL is met by the recipient's ability to replace the file. Rust crates are linked into Lattice's executable and npm packages into its bundle; an LGPL licence there would oblige Lattice to hand out a relinkable form of its own build, which the commercial licence cannot, so for them the LGPL stays 'review'. An entry here may also name a whole 'ID WITH exception' leaf, which then wins over the base licence's category.
$comment_denied: GPL/AGPL from third parties would remove the commercial licence option; the others restrict use or field.
$comment_types: Licence type shown in the 'Licences by type' summary of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md. Every licence in 'allowed' and 'obligation' must have one. OFL-1.1 is listed as weak copyleft: modified fonts must stay under the OFL, documents using them are unaffected.
$comment_preference: For 'A OR B' the best category wins; among equals, a licence whose text the package ships wins (so its own copyright text is reproduced), then the licence listed first here. MIT first: short per-copy text that recipients know. Public-domain dedications (CC0, Unlicense) last: their effect is uncertain in jurisdictions without a public-domain waiver.

clarifications.name: khroma
clarifications.reason: package.json has no license field; the shipped 'license' file is the MIT licence text. A new version or a changed file fails the gate until re-checked.

exceptions.name: libdbus-1-3
exceptions.reason: D-Bus is GPL-2.0-or-later OR AFL-2.1 at the recipient's choice. Lattice's AGPL distribution uses it under GPL-2.0-or-later (upgradable to GPL-3.0, combinable with the AGPL); the commercial licence uses AFL-2.1, which the FSF considers GPL-incompatible. No single option fits both outbound licences, so the policy model needs this exception. Version '*': a Debian package is pinned by the hash of its copyright file in foss/appimage-packages.json instead. Re-check with legal review before it expires.
